questions.explain: In Case Study 1 (trade-sentinel), validation requires the synchronous secondary to be SYNCHRONIZED with a redo queue under 512KB and healthy quorum; if either fails the daemon escalates to PagerDuty and holds without failing over.
options: Fail over immediately to avoid downtime
Confirm the sync secondary is SYNCHRONIZED with redo queue under 512KB and quorum is healthy; otherwise escalate and hold
Wait for three business days
Drop the heartbeat table
questions.q: What validation gates must pass before trade-sentinel initiates an autonomous failover?

questions.explain: The SaaS analytics agent applies REBUILD ONLINE when fragmentation > 30% and page count > 1000, REORGANIZE when fragmentation > 10% and page count > 500, skips small tables, and defers rebuilds estimated over 4 minutes to the tenant's local 2-6 AM maintenance window.
options: Rebuild everything every night
Reorganize only, never rebuild
Use Ola Hallengren's solution unchanged
Rebuild online if fragmentation > 30% and pages > 1000; reorganize if > 10% and pages > 500; defer > 4-minute rebuilds to the tenant's local off-peak window
questions.q: What decision logic does the autonomous index agent use in the SaaS case study?

questions.explain: The e-commerce autoscaler uses asymmetric cooldowns — 60 seconds for scale-up, 300 seconds for scale-down — and sheds load first (throttling background jobs) before scaling, because a symmetric cooldown caused premature scale-down and immediate re-scale flapping.
options: Symmetric 60-second cooldowns in both directions
Never scale down, only scale up
An asymmetric cooldown (60s scale-up, 300s scale-down) and shedding load before scaling
Scale up only when CPU hits 100%
questions.q: What two operational refinements did the e-commerce autonomous scaling deployment learn?

questions.explain: After the agent silently revoked an EXECUTE permission on an undocumented stored procedure relied on by a batch job, Tier 1 actions were scoped to a pre-approved Compliance.Tier1EligibleObjects registry reviewed quarterly.
options: Tier 1 actions now require the affected object to appear in a pre-approved Tier1EligibleObjects registry reviewed quarterly
All Tier 1 actions were disabled permanently
The audit log was deleted
Compliance violations are no longer remediated automatically
questions.q: What refinement followed the compliance agent's silent batch-job failure in Case Study 5?

questions.explain: The chapter's synthesis lists five patterns: layered decision gates (no single threshold triggers irreversible change), audit-first act-second, asymmetric conservatism, human override surfaces without override requirements, and production failure as design input.
options: Single thresholds can directly trigger destructive changes
Layered decision gates, audit-first act-second, asymmetric conservatism, human override surfaces, and production failure as design input
Automation should always be maximally aggressive
Human approval must gate every action
questions.q: Which pattern best summarizes the cross-case-study synthesis of production-surviving autonomous DBA systems?
